description: We are apart of a High School Technology team that is interested in Robotics and Artificial intelligence and we are ready to improve
summary:
The search for extrasolar planets has entered a golden age, with NASA missions like Kepler and TESS generating unprecedented volumes of stellar photometric data. However, analyzing these massive datasets to detect subtle transit signals—where a planet dims its host star—creates a massive bottleneck for professional astronomers. Existing astronomical analysis tools are overly complex, steep in learning curves, and completely inaccessible to students, educators, and everyday space enthusiasts.

To bridge this gap, we present ExoPulse, an interactive, open-source web platform that democratizes exoplanet discovery. ExoPulse ingests authentic light curve data directly from NASA archives through a lightweight Python backend, transforming raw data into intuitive, visual graphs. The platform features an interactive analytics dashboard where users can examine stellar brightness variations, spot transit dips, and engage in crowdsourced anomaly detection. Furthermore, ExoPulse includes an automated Habitability Engine that calculates whether candidate planets reside within the circumstellar habitable zone. By merging scalable data processing with human-powered pattern recognition, ExoPulse transforms global space fans into active citizen scientists, accelerating the quest for potentially habitable alien worlds.
details:
1. Background & The Problem

The exponential growth of space telescope missions (such as NASA's Kepler, K2, and TESS) has unlocked an unprecedented era of exoplanet discovery. However, these missions produce massive volumes of photometric data—specifically, light curves tracking stellar brightness over time. Detecting planetary transits (when a planet crosses in front of its host star, causing a periodic dip in brightness) within this ocean of data creates a massive bottleneck for professional researchers. While existing citizen science initiatives (e.g., Planet Hunters) crowdsource data analysis, their interfaces are often disjointed, lack real-time contextual feedback, and fail to educate users on why a candidate is scientifically significant. Consequently, students and space enthusiasts are treated as passive clickers rather than active scientific analysts.

2. Detailed Solution & Architecture

ExoPulse solves this by bridging raw astronomical datasets with an intuitive, gamified, and educational web application. The platform is structured into three core pillars:

  • A. Data Ingestion & Automated Pipeline:
      1. Light Curve View: Zoomable scatter plot showing stellar flux over time.
      2. Phase-Folded View: Aligns multiple transit periods to confirm signal periodicity and eliminate false positives (such as eclipsing binary stars).
  • Includes crowdsourced flagging buttons allowing users to categorize light curves into "High-Probability Transit," "Eclipsing Binary," or "Noise."
  • C. Automated Habitability Engine:
  • Unlike conventional tools that only detect transits, ExoPulse calculates the exoplanet's physical viability in real time.
  • Integrates stellar effective temperature ($T_{eff}$) and estimated orbital semi-major axis ($a$) to compute the star's circumstellar habitable zone (the "Goldilocks Zone").
  • Instantly outputs an interactive "Habitability Index" badge showing whether the candidate orbits within a temperature regime suitable for liquid water.

3. Technology Stack

  • Data Processing & Backend: Python, Pandas, AstroPy, NumPy
  • Analytics & Visualization: Matplotlib, Plotly (for interactive zoomable charts)
  • User Interface / Dashboard: Streamlit (ideal for fast, high-performance 48-hour deployment)
  • Data Sources: NASA Exoplanet Archive, NASA MAST Portal

4. Impact & Future Roadmap

ExoPulse transforms passive space enthusiasts into contributing citizen scientists by gamifying astrophysical data analysis. By combining automated noise filtering with human pattern recognition and automated habitability scoring, ExoPulse accelerates exoplanet candidate validation while making space exploration accessible to classrooms worldwide. Future Roadmap: Implementing a lightweight machine learning classification model to pre-train users on recognizing complex transit shapes.
